answer: DeepWalk trains a skip-gram model on node sequences generated by random walks, so its objective is to predict nodes that appear within a fixed context window around each node. That means the model only learns useful co-occurrence statistics if the walks are long enough to produce many overlapping local contexts and enough repeated node pairs. With short walks, especially on sparse graphs, there are too few training pairs and the sampled contexts are dominated by very local neighborhoods, so the embeddings do not capture the broader graph structure well. Increasing the walk length far beyond the fixed value used in the Flickr and BlogCatalog experiments gives the skip-gram objective many more context pairs and lets information propagate farther through the graph, which is why performance improves only when walks are made much longer.
